newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Modelo opens big new brewery.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Modelo opens big new brewery.

text.p: Gerardo Ruvalcaba Seanez, a chemical engineer and professional beer-taster for Mexican brewer Grupo Modelo SA, closed his eyes and took a deep sip of Corona.
"This is perfect," the quality control expert said, placing his cold beer back on the factory bar.
He had a look of satisfaction on his face, one that was familiar here Tuesday at Grupo Modelo's brand new plant in Zacatecas state.
One day after the formal inauguration Monday, company officials did little to hide their enthusiasm for the new plant during an interview with Reuters.
After all, Modelo built the $356 million plant with its own cash reserves over five years, barely making a dent in quarterly earnings along the way.

The factory's tall silos stand out for miles on an otherwise barren plane about 20 miles (30 km) outside the city of Zacatecas. Inside, shiny stainless steel vats and tubes contain beer in the making, as evidenced by the powerful smell of cooking grains.

Modelo officials boast that the Zacatecas plant is the most modern in the world. After three phases of expansion over the next five years, it also will be the fifth-largest beer factory in the world and the largest in Latin America, they said.

Beverage analysts from the most important brokerages in New York and Mexico City will be keeping a close watch on the new plant. With the Corona brand gaining a foothold in markets the world over, Grupo Modelo is one of Mexico's most successful companies and a blue chip on the Mexican stock exchange.

The new plant, Modelo's eighth, gives Modelo the latest edge in the beer wars with competitor Fomento Economico Mexicano (FEMSA), analysts said. But FEMSA, the brewer of Tecate, Dos Equis, Carta Blanca and other brands, is keeping pace by boosting capacity at its seven existing plants.
The main concern of financial markets is whether the additional production from the new plant could lead to a drop in prices, or even a price war with FEMSA.
Carlos Fernandez, vice president of Grupo Modelo's board of directors, attempted to allay those fears on Tuesday.
"This does not represent a increase in the supply of the product so much as additional production to meet the demands of the market," Fernandez said. "We won't have an excess of production."
When asked specifically about whether there would be a price war, he said, "Not initiated by us."

The Zacatecas plant, which produced its first beer for sale March 14, begins production with an annual capacity of about 3.5 million hectoliters. A hectoliter, the unit of measure used by the industry, is 100 liters, the equivalent of a little more than three kegs of beer.

By the end of next year, Fernandez said, the second phase could come on line, doubling capacity. Two additional expansions after that will boost capacity to at least 14 million hectoliters, more than half the company's 1996 sales volumes of 27.38 million hectoliters.

Company officials backed up the claim that the plant is the most modern in the world by pointing to the computerized production system that has a bank of engineers punching in commands on a keyboard instead of turning valves on the production floor.

Modelo makes 10 brands led by its wildly successful Corona label, which spearheaded export growth of 28 percent in 1996 to 3.7 million hectoliters, a figure that has doubled over the past three years.
Company officials said the Zacatecas plant will be used exclusively for domestic production, taking some of the production demands off its other factories used for export.

Perhaps the crowning glory for the new plant came on Monday when Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo came to the inauguration. He brought along two friends -- the king and queen of Spain -- who made last-minute alterations in their travel plans so that they could attend.
They were told that the plant was designed and built entirely by Mexicans, an obvious source of local pride.

"I remember when people said that you had to be foreign, German, in order to make beer," Grupo Modelo technical director Salvador Lopez said. "Yesterday (when the special guests arrived) I was thinking just that."
